Sometimes you want a passage gone but not the time it occupies — a phone ringing under a pause, a name you need to bleep. Silencing keeps the clip exactly as long as it was and only flattens the selected part.

:::note[Coming from Audacity?]
This is Audacity's **Edit → Remove Special → Silence Audio**. The names below are Soundscaper's own, which sometimes differ.
:::

## Steps

1. Open Soundscaper. A new, empty project is ready as soon as the editor loads.
2. Choose **File → Import audio** and pick your recording. This lesson uses `lesson-music-loop.wav`. The file lands as a clip on its own track.
3. Drag in the ruler above the clip, from the 40% mark to the 60% mark of the clip, to select that range. Select just the part you want to mute.
4. Choose **Edit → Remove special → Silence audio**.
5. The project now shows 1 clip.
   *You should see:* The waveform is flat across the selection and the clip is still one piece.

## Tips

- Silence is a normal edit: **Edit → Undo** brings the audio back.
- To remove the time as well as the sound, see [Cut a mistake out of a recording](/lessons/cut-out-a-mistake/).

## About this lesson

Every step on this page is replayed against each build of Soundscaper by the browser suite (`tests/browser/soundscaper-lessons.spec.js`). If a menu entry, field or button stops matching, the build fails until the lesson is corrected, so the steps you read are the steps the editor accepts.
